propositions: The gate's _collect_reads builds a global set of bare attribute names read anywhere in src/rebar, allowing any field whose name appears on any unrelated config object to pass the gate regardless of whether that specific field is ever read.

A field is falsely satisfied when a same-named attribute on an unrelated config is read, causing the gate to miss inert fields with common names like 'enabled', 'path', or 'timeout' that are reused across multiple dataclasses.

The fix must resolve each read to its owning dataclass via receiver expression analysis (section names, annotations, assignments, return types, branches, and cross-module call sites) rather than matching bare terminal names globally.

Four fields are newly flagged by the corrected gate and must receive accurate `# read-via:` markers citing their real readers: McpConfig.readonly, McpConfig.allow_llm, McpConfig.allow_jira_sync, and JiraConfig.allow_insecure—none require product triage because all are traced to live consumers.

Both test files must be migrated to the owner-resolution contract with resolvable receivers (section fields, annotations, aliases) rather than worked around, and a RED-first synthetic test must prove the old gate false-negatives an inert field reusing a common name.
The gate must report any existing `# read-via:` marker naming a rebar ticket id so markers parked against closed tickets surface rather than silently persist.
